bank.question: Before conducting a Stop and Search under Section 1 of PACE, an officer must inform the individual which police station the officer is based at

bank.explanation: Under the Code of Ethics, 'Fitness for Work' means officers must ensure they are mentally and physically fit to carry out their duties safely

bank.explanation: The Code of Ethics applies to all police personnel, including civilian staff, volunteers, and those off-duty if their conduct affects the force's reputation
bank.question: The College of Policing Code of Ethics applies only to warranted police officers and not to civilian police staff

bank.explanation: Section 17 of PACE allows entry without a warrant to arrest for an indictable offence or to protect life and limb or prevent serious damage to property
bank.question: Under Section 17 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act (PACE), an officer can enter a property without a warrant to arrest for an indictable offence
In a criminal trial in England and Wales, the prosecution bears the burden of proving the defendant's guilt
bank.explanation: The 'burden of proof' rests with the prosecution to prove the defendant is guilty beyond reasonable doubt
Officers can be required to work overtime or change shifts at short notice to meet operational demands and emergencies
bank.question: Police officers have a legal right to refuse to work any overtime that was not scheduled at least 48 hours in advance

bank.explanation: The GOWISELY acronym mandates that officers provide their name, station, and the legal grounds for the search before starting

bank.question: A police officer's primary duty at a dangerous scene is to ensure their own personal safety above all other considerations, including public safety
bank.explanation: The primary duty is to protect the public and preserve life; they should not take unnecessary risks that would incapacitate them from helping

bank.question: Victims of crime have the right to make a Victim Personal Statement to explain how the crime has impacted them
bank.explanation: Victim Personal Statements allow victims to explain how the crime has affected their lives physically, emotionally, or financially

bank.question: An officer can lawfully conduct a stop and search based solely on the fact that a person has a previous criminal conviction

bank.explanation: Under Section 24 of PACE, an officer may arrest someone without a warrant if they have reasonable grounds to suspect they are committing an offence

bank.question: Police Community Support Officers (PCSOs) have different legal powers compared to warranted police officers

bank.explanation: Police officers are expected to maintain professional standards of behavior both on and off duty to uphold public confidence in the service

bank.question: During a Stop and Search, an officer must explain the 'grounds' (the legal reason) for the search to the individual

bank.explanation: Section 24 of PACE (as amended) allows an arrest without a warrant if an officer has reasonable grounds to suspect an offence has been committed
bank.question: A police officer can arrest a person if they have reasonable grounds to suspect that the person has committed a criminal offence

bank.explanation: Under the Equality Act 2010, gender reassignment is a protected characteristic, and discrimination on this basis is unlawful
bank.question: Under the Equality Act 2010, gender reassignment is not listed as a protected characteristic
When using force, a police officer's actions must be 'proportionate, legal, and necessary' under the circumstances
bank.explanation: Reasonableness is a subjective and objective test based on the officer's honest belief and the necessity of the force used in the circumstances

bank.question: A police officer is legally allowed to wait up to 48 hours before recording their initial notes about a crime scene
bank.explanation: Evidence should be recorded immediately or as soon as practicable to ensure accuracy and satisfy the court's requirements for 'contemporaneous' notes
The Custody Officer is a sergeant or above who is independent of the investigation and responsible for the welfare of detainees
bank.question: The 'Custody Officer' is responsible for overseeing the welfare of people held in police cells
Police officers are required to turn off their Body Worn Video (BWV) cameras whenever a member of the public asks them to
bank.explanation: Body Worn Video is used to provide an objective record of encounters, assisting both the investigation and the accountability of the officer
While they have the right to silence, the court can be invited to draw a 'negative inference' if they later rely on a fact they failed to mention
bank.question: During a police interview, a suspect has the right to remain silent, but this may harm their defence if the case goes to court
If the police receive information that someone's life is in immediate danger, they have no legal obligation to intervene
bank.explanation: The police have a positive obligation under the Human Rights Act 1998 to take reasonable steps to protect a person whose life is at risk

bank.question: A person suspected of a standard criminal offence can generally be held in police custody for up to 24 hours before they must be charged or released

bank.question: Police officers are required to report any personal involvement in a civil or criminal legal matter to their Professional Standards Department
An officer conducting a stop and search is not legally required to tell the person what item they are looking for until after the search is complete

The Code of Ethics applies to all police personnel at all times, as their off-duty conduct can impact the reputation of the police service
bank.question: The police 'Code of Ethics' applies to officers both when they are on duty and during their private lives

bank.explanation: Officers have a positive legal obligation (the 'Osman' warning) to take reasonable steps to protect a person's life if they are aware of a real and immediate threat
bank.question: Police have a 'positive obligation' under the Human Rights Act to take steps to protect a person's life if they are aware of a specific threat to it

bank.explanation: While BWV provides crucial evidence, an officer's written statement remains a primary legal record and is still a mandatory requirement for most incidents
bank.question: If an entire incident is captured on Body Worn Video, the attending officer is no longer required to write a formal witness statement or pocketbook entry

bank.explanation: Officers must use the minimum amount of force required to achieve a lawful objective, ensuring it is balanced against the threat faced

bank.question: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is an external body that oversees complaints made against police forces in England and Wales
bank.explanation: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is a non-departmental public body that oversees the police complaints system independently of the police

bank.question: A suspect in a police interview has the right to consult a solicitor privately, and this advice is provided free of charge if they use the duty solicitor
bank.explanation: Any person being interviewed under caution has the legal right to free and independent legal advice, regardless of their financial status

bank.question: When making an arrest, a police officer must inform the person that they are under arrest and the grounds for that arrest, even if the fact of the arrest is obvious
bank.explanation: Under the PACE Code of Practice, officers must inform the person that they are under arrest and state the specific legal grounds for that arrest as soon as is practicable
